outline: This course introduces fundamental statistical concepts and analytical tools for data-driven decision-making. Core topics cover descriptive statistics, data visualization, basic probability theory, random variable distributions, inferential statistics (hypothesis testing and confidence intervals for numerical and categorical data), and simple linear regression. The curriculum emphasizes building conceptual intuition and practical application in English. This course is offered under the Taiwan AI College Alliance (TAICA) program. Lectures are delivered asynchronously by NTU faculty via NTU COOL.
schedule:
* Course Introduction & Data Fundamentals
* Data Types, Sampling Methods, and Experimental Design
* Summarizing Data Numerical & Graphical Representations
* Basic Probability Rules, Conditional Probability, and Independence
* Random Variables, Normal Distribution, and Binomial Distribution
* Sampling Distributions and Central Limit Theorem
* Confidence Intervals and Point Estimates
* Midterm Exam (Synchronized, In-Person 9:30 AM – 12:00 PM)
* Hypothesis Testing for Single Categorical Proportions
* Chi-Square Tests for Independence and Goodness-of-Fit
* Hypothesis Testing & Confidence Intervals for Single Means
* Comparing Two Independent Means and Paired Data Analysis
* Introduction to Simple Linear Regression & Correlation
* Model Fitting, Least Squares Method, and Residual Analysis
* Final Exam (Synchronized, In-Person 9:30 AM – 12:00 PM)
* Course Review & Final Grade Assessment

flexible_learning.content: Weeks 17 and 18 focus on statistical problem-solving, regression model interpretation, and data analysis synthesis. Students will work on guided problem sets involving probability calculations, confidence interval construction, and linear regression evaluations
flexible_learning.outcome: Student performance is evaluated through practice problem submissions, participation in statistical exercise discussions, and self-review reports on regression and inference concepts.
